title: Es creada la Universidad Autónoma de Chihuahua (UACH) a través del decreto 171 del gobernador Oscar Soto Maynez. La universidad inició actividades con las escuelas de medicina, Ingeniería, Derecho, Educación física y Farmacia.
text: Óscar Soto Maynez fue un abogado y político mexicano, miembro del Partido Revolucionario Institucional. Fue gobernador de Chihuahua entre 1950 y 1955.

title: The Museo Regional de la Ceramica, Tlaquepaque is established in Tlaquepaque, Jalisco.
text: The Museo Regional de la Cerámica in Tlaquepaque, Jalisco, Mexico is located on Independencia Street in the center of the city. The museum is one of two main ceramics museums in the city, with the other being the Pantaleon Panduro Museum .

title: The Confederación Revolucionaria de Trabajadores is founded.
text: Confederación Revolucionaria de Trabajadores is a trade union centre in Mexico. Mario Suárez has served as the general secretary of CRT for many years.

title: Hurricane Alice (June 1954)
text: Hurricane Alice was the second-strongest Atlantic hurricane to make landfall in the month of June since reliable records began in the 1850s. The storm was linked to catastrophic flooding in southern Texas and northern Mexico, especially along the Rio Grande and its tributaries.

title: The Autonomous University of Chihuahua is founded.
text: The Autonomous University of Chihuahua is a Mexican public university based in the city of Chihuahua, Chihuahua, but with several campuses across the state. On December 8, 1954, the State Legislature, with Governor Oscar Soto Maynez, issued the decree 171, which founded the Autonomous University of Chihuahua (UACh).

title: 1954 Carrera Panamericana.
text: The 1954 Carrera Panamericana was the fifth and final running of the Carrera Panamericana Mexican sports car racing event, run from November 19–23, 1954. It was the sixth and final race of the 1954 World Sportscar Championship.

title: The 1954 Central American and Caribbean Games are held in Mexico City.
text: The seventh Central American and Caribbean Games were held in Mexico City, the capital city of Mexico. The games were held from the 5 March to the 20 March 1954, and included 1,356 athletes from twelve nations.

title: The United States defeat Mexico in the Americas Zone final of the Davis Cup.
text: The 1954 Davis Cup was the 43rd edition of the Davis Cup, the most important tournament between national teams in men's tennis. 23 teams entered the Europe Zone and 7 teams entered the America Zone.

title: The Tecolotes de Nuevo Laredo win the Mexican League.
text: The Tecolotes de los Dos Laredos, formerly known as the Tecolotes de Nuevo Laredo (English: Nuevo Laredo Owls), are a professional baseball team in the Mexican League. The Tecolotes are a binational baseball team, splitting their home games between Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas, Mexico and Laredo, Texas, United States.

title: Club Celaya is founded.
text: Celaya Fútbol Club, was a professional football club based in Celaya, Guanajuato. The club competed in Liga Premier, the third level of Mexican football, and played its home matches at Estadio Miguel Alemán Valdés.
